events.F5-01.name: The Bell That Rings Twice
events.F5-01.scene: The town bell rings twice with a single pull. The clapper swings back against the rim, causing the watch to mistake the signals.
events.F5-01.action: Leave some slack in the return cord and ask someone below the bell tower to signal a single strike.
events.F5-01.result: The bell rings just once. The gatekeeper pays you 760G for the repair.
events.F5-02.name: The Outer Moat Gauge
events.F5-02.scene: The drainage keeper is troubled because the water level never seems to return to normal. Mud beneath the gauge board is pushing it sideways.
events.F5-02.action: Remove the mud, stand the board upright, and align it with the reference line on the stone.
events.F5-02.result: The keeper can read the correct water level again. Receive 580G for your help.
events.F5-03.name: The Rivet Hiding the Address
events.F5-03.scene: No one can read where an arriving shipment belongs. A large-headed rivet securing its tag sits right over the district number.
events.F5-03.action: Remove the tag and punch a new hole in its corner to leave the number visible.
events.F5-03.result: The carts leave for their correct gates. Receive 460G for sorting the shipments.
events.F5-04.name: The Drawbridge’s Last Tooth
events.F5-04.scene: The drawbridge stops partway down, with its final tooth failing to mesh with the gear. A line of carts is growing outside the castle.
events.F5-04.action: Support the bridge, align the displaced toothed plate with its neighbor, and tighten it.
events.F5-04.result: The bridge lowers all the way. The castle works office pays you 1000G for the emergency repair.
events.F5-05.name: The Granary’s Measuring Pan
events.F5-05.scene: Grain spills from the edge of the measuring pan, throwing off the month-end stock count. Pressing a cloth along the rim reveals a crack.
events.F5-05.action: Secure a patch over the crack and measure the same scoop again.
events.F5-05.result: Each load measures consistently. The granary keeper pays you 690G.
events.F5-06.name: Sharpening Samples at the Main Gate
events.F5-06.scene: A sharpener outside the main gate displays a chipped blade beside a properly sharpened one. Under the light, the chips leave scattered points of reflection.
events.F5-06.action: Choose the blade with reflected dots to finish, or work on the blade without them.
events.F5-06.result: Finishing the dotted blade removes its chips and earns you SW41. The craftsperson takes back the undamaged blade with no reward.
events.F5-07.name: A Trial Beside the Castle Wall
events.F5-07.scene: The wall-side workshop has prepared rope-cutting and wooden-shield striking tests. The craftsperson offers you the sword used in whichever test you undertake.
events.F5-07.action: Take the rope-cutting test or the wooden-shield test.
events.F5-07.result: The rope test grants SW42. The wooden-shield test costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grants SW43.
events.F5-08.name: Pulling Nails from the Old Gate
events.F5-08.scene: Removing nails from an old gate reveals an armory tag on its back. You will be rewarded for the work if you leave that surface unmarked.
events.F5-08.action: Place scrap wood under your tool before pulling the nails, or brace the tool directly against the gate.
events.F5-08.result: The scrap wood protects the gate and earns you SW44. Bracing directly against it leaves damage to repair and grants nothing.
events.F5-09.name: Two Colors of Sealing Thread
events.F5-09.scene: The armory inspector has tied different-colored sealing threads around two swords. One is ready to hand over; the other requires your help with inspection.
events.F5-09.action: Choose the inspected sword with white thread, or help inspect the one with red thread.
events.F5-09.result: White grants SW45. Red costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grants SW46.
events.F5-10.name: The Thin Blade Washer
events.F5-10.scene: Replacement washers lie on a bench by the gate. One is too thin and rattles, but adding the second closes the gap in the blade fastener.
events.F5-10.action: Stack both washers and check the blade, or return the second washer to the craftsperson.
events.F5-10.result: Stacking both passes the adjustment test and grants SW47. Returning one leaves the prototype in the workshop.
events.F5-11.name: The Outer Moat Returns Window
events.F5-11.scene: A departing garrison has returned one weapon and one piece of armor. Help carry them, and you may keep either one.
events.F5-11.action: Go to the weapon shelf or armor shelf and register which reward you want.
events.F5-11.result: The weapon shelf grants SW48; the armor shelf grants AR41. The garrison keeps the other.
events.F5-12.name: The Master’s Final Mark
events.F5-12.scene: An elderly master wants to stamp his mark on his final sword. His usual anvil is too low to stamp straight while standing.
events.F5-12.action: Raise the work surface to the height of his workshop chair and support it so he can stamp the mark himself.
events.F5-12.result: The master stamps his own mark and gives you the finished SW49 in thanks.
events.F5-13.name: The Royal Workshop’s Price Tags
events.F5-13.scene: A celebrated royal sword rests on the upper shelf, with an apprentice’s prototype below. The upper tag reads 3000G; the lower says, “Yours if you help test it.”
events.F5-13.action: Buy the celebrated sword for 3000G, or test the lower sword against a practice target.
events.F5-13.result: Buying costs 3000G and grants SW50. Testing costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grants SW42. You can test it even without enough gold to buy.
events.F5-14.name: Crouching at the Arrow Slit
events.F5-14.scene: Armor for defenders using low arrow slits must not lift at the edges when they crouch. Light slips through the edge of the sample.
events.F5-14.action: Shift the strap until the light no longer shows, then check again while seated.
events.F5-14.result: Receive AR42 for passing the inspection.
events.F5-15.name: The Shield Rack’s Width
events.F5-15.scene: Equipment scrapes against one side of a storage rack whenever it is returned. The partitions differ in spacing by a finger’s width.
events.F5-15.action: Move the partition on the narrow side, or collect your reward at another, wider rack.
events.F5-15.result: Fixing the partition grants AR43. Using the other rack grants AR44.
events.F5-16.name: Basting the Battle Uniform
events.F5-16.scene: The castle tailor uses bright thread for temporary stitches. Red loops are basting; black stitches are the finished seams.
events.F5-16.action: Remove only the red loops and try it on, or pull the black stitches.
events.F5-16.result: Removing red finishes the piece and grants AR45. Pulling black means it must be resewn, with no reward.
events.F5-17.name: Footwork on the Stone Steps
events.F5-17.scene: Before entering the castle, you can test equipment fasteners with one foot on a low step. The examiner demonstrates two tests.
events.F5-17.action: Choose a light, step-by-step test or climb the steps carrying a load.
events.F5-17.result: The light test grants AR46. Carrying a load costs 3 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grants AR47.
events.F5-18.name: The Barracks Care-Package Shelf
events.F5-18.scene: A care-package shelf in town seeks donations of combat supplies. Supporters can receive serviced armor in return.
events.F5-18.action: Donate one AT41, contribute 440G toward a care package, or pass.
events.F5-18.result: Consume one AT41 or pay 440G to receive AR48. Giving neither leaves everything unchanged.
events.F5-19.name: Relief Patterns on the Drain Covers
events.F5-19.scene: New drain covers have been installed in the castle square. You may copy a pattern from the old covers onto armor: a band or a circle around a central point.
events.F5-19.action: Copy the band pattern, or finish the armor to match the circular pattern.
events.F5-19.result: The band grants AR49; the circle grants AR50. Take home only one design.
events.F5-20.name: An Oil Passage in the Hinge
events.F5-20.scene: Oil is not reaching the armory door’s hinge shaft, making the door hard to open. Clearing sand from the top reveals a small oil hole.
events.F5-20.action: Brush away the sand, oil the small hole, then open the door and choose your reward.
events.F5-20.result: Choose a weapon for SW44 or armor for AR42.
events.F5-21.name: The Final White-Cloth Inspection
events.F5-21.scene: An inspector at the castle gate runs white cloth along an armor edge. A tiny projection catches and frays the cloth.
events.F5-21.action: File down the projection and finish this piece, or exchange it for inspected stock.
events.F5-21.result: Finishing grants AR48. Choosing stock consumes one BD41 and grants AR49. You can finish the piece without BD41.
events.F5-22.name: Rainwater from the Rampart
events.F5-22.scene: A Rampart Gargoyle lands on a stone basin collecting rain. Opening a drainage valve could release the water just as it makes its first dive.
events.F5-22.action: Take charge of the valve and prepare for the dive, or return it to the drainage keeper and fight.
events.F5-22.result: Fight EN08. With the valve, guarding against its first dive makes it slip and reduces that hit’s damage by an additional 6. Returning the valve gives a normal battle. Victory grants enemy-specific XP and gold, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.F5-23.name: Threads on the Moat Bridge
events.F5-23.scene: A Thorn Spider has spun webs on the bridge chains. A thick chain could stop its charge; a thin hauling rope could draw it closer.
events.F5-23.action: Use the thick chain as a shield, or fight holding the thin rope.
events.F5-23.result: Fight EN07. With the thick chain, guarding on your first turn reduces the enemy’s first direct hit by an additional 6. With the thin rope, a normal attack that hits on your first turn deals 4 extra damage. Victory grants enemy-specific XP and gold, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.F5-24.name: Above the Parapet, Below the Floor
events.F5-24.scene: A work crew outside the castle needs inspectors for the parapet and the space beneath the floor. Stone wings wait above; unbroken webs lie below.
events.F5-24.action: Join the parapet inspection or enter beneath the floor.
events.F5-24.result: Fight one normal battle against EN08 at the parapet or EN07 beneath the floor. Victory grants enemy-specific XP and gold, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.F5-25.name: The Roof Ornament to Recarve
events.F5-25.scene: As a tiler tries to remove a roof ornament, a nearby Rampart Gargoyle turns around. Climbing down the scaffolding would let you abandon the job.
events.F5-25.action: Protect the tiler and fight, or retreat to safe scaffolding.
events.F5-25.result: Protecting the tiler starts a battle against EN08. Retreating lets you continue without a battle or reward. Victory grants enemy-specific XP and gold, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.F5-26.name: The Padded Weapon Crate
events.F5-26.scene: A Thorn Spider has slipped into the padding inside a weapon crate at the outer moat supply post. The quartermaster sells supplies for the approach to the castle.
events.F5-26.action: Buy AT42 for 194G before opening the crate, or open it without buying.
events.F5-26.result: Buying costs 194G and grants one AT42. Fight EN07 inside the crate even if you decline or cannot afford the purchase. Victory grants enemy-specific XP and gold, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.F5-27.name: The Statue Awaiting Dawn
events.F5-27.scene: A Rampart Gargoyle in the bridge’s shadow spreads its wings when the bell sounds the hour. It cannot see you while you wait for the bell.
events.F5-27.action: Prepare your guard until the bell rings, or enter the bridge’s shadow early.
events.F5-27.result: Fight EN08. If you wait and guard on your first turn, your first normal attack to hit in the next round deals 6 extra damage. Entering early instead adds 3 damage only to a normal attack that hits on your first turn. Victory grants enemy-specific XP and gold, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.F5-28.name: The Mist’s Trick Curtain
events.F5-28.scene: Several wolf silhouettes appear on a thin curtain at the worksite. Only one row of fresh footprints marks the soil behind it.
events.F5-28.action: Challenge the powerful foe and use the footprints to find its real body, or lower the curtain and continue through the side gate.
events.F5-28.result: Challenging starts a battle against MB03. A normal attack on your first turn deals 5 extra damage only if it hits the real body with footprints. Lowering the curtain gives no battle or reward. Victory grants enemy-specific XP and gold, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. You cannot flee after challenging. Losing grants no battle rewards.
events.F5-29.name: The Last Shipment at the Gate
events.F5-29.scene: The next shipment has reached town. A smith sets down two crates and asks, “Something for the coming fight, or something for the road to the castle?”
events.F5-29.action: Open either the battle crate or the travel crate.
events.F5-29.result: The battle crate grants one AT43; the travel crate grants one BD42.
events.F5-30.name: The Fire Bucket’s Inner Lid
events.F5-30.scene: A medical pouch is tied to the inner lid of a fire bucket. A blue cord holds the pouch; a red cord connects to the water-release plug.
events.F5-30.action: Pull the blue cord or reach for the red cord.
events.F5-30.result: Blue grants one HE41. The watchman stops you from pulling red, and you continue empty-handed.
events.F5-31.name: The Outer Moat Signboard
events.F5-31.scene: One signboard needs replacing before the gate closes. A shelf accepting travel supplies faces another offering combat supplies.
events.F5-31.action: Trade one BD43 for a combat item, or simply replace the signboard.
events.F5-31.result: Trading consumes one BD43 and grants one AT44. Simply replacing the board restores 3 HP. You can replace it without the item.
events.F5-32.name: Marks on the Patrol Bags
events.F5-32.scene: The aid station needs someone to stamp patrol bags. The stamp determines which supply you can take home.
events.F5-32.action: Choose a cross or an arrow and stamp a set of bags.
events.F5-32.result: A cross grants one HE42; an arrow grants one BD44.
events.F5-33.name: A Wheelbarrow Carrying a Door
events.F5-33.scene: A wheelbarrow loaded with a removed door has its handles resting on the ground. With two people, one can steady the door while the other wheels it away.
events.F5-33.action: Take the handles in place of the craftsperson, or walk beside the barrow and steady the door.
events.F5-33.result: Wheeling it costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grants one AT45. Steadying it grants one HE43.
events.F5-34.name: Steam at the Ration Window
events.F5-34.scene: At the final distribution, separate lines form for a warm drink here and medical supplies to take away.
events.F5-34.action: Collect a package at the takeaway window, or join the hot-water line for a drink.
events.F5-34.result: Taking a package grants one HE44. Drinking restores 4 MP but grants no item.
events.F5-35.name: Rice Cakes on the Iron Plate
events.F5-35.scene: Rice cakes are cooking on an iron plate taken off the fire for everyone who helped with the castle works. You may choose how browned yours should be.
events.F5-35.action: Eat a rice cake, or share tea with the person serving them and catch your breath.
events.F5-35.result: A rice cake restores 12 HP. Tea restores 4 HP and 4 MP.
events.F5-36.name: Leather Pillows for Tired Arms
events.F5-36.scene: A tailor has sewn two small leather pillows for those who have spent too long gripping a sword. Rest your arms on them or lie down.
events.F5-36.action: Rest your arms and close your eyes, or take off your shoes and lie down.
events.F5-36.result: Resting your arms restores 6 MP. Lying down restores 10 HP and 1 MP.
events.F5-37.name: A Bath in the Castle’s Shadow
events.F5-37.scene: Water drawn from the outer moat has been heated in a separate tank for bathing. The attendant offers a free footbath or a paid full bath.
events.F5-37.action: Take the footbath, or pay 180G for a full bath.
events.F5-37.result: The footbath restores 6 HP. A full bath costs 180G and restores 14 HP and 2 MP. You can take the footbath without enough gold.
events.F5-38.name: The Watch Change Hourglass
events.F5-38.scene: Until the watchman’s hourglass runs out, a quiet seat is free inside the castle wall. You can rest before your final preparations.
events.F5-38.action: Breathe in time with the hourglass and rest your hands until the sand runs out.
events.F5-38.result: Restore 7 HP and 4 MP before the next watch takes the seat.
events.F5-39.name: The Gate Rivet Inn
events.F5-39.scene: An inn uses a large gate rivet as its sign. Swordsmiths and travelers bound for the castle make their final preparations here.
events.F5-39.action: Pass under the rivet sign and choose the fireside room, shop, worktable, or companions’ seating. Ask the master about the Demon King’s swordplay.
events.F5-39.result: Rest in the fireside room, shop, change jobs at the worktable, or recruit companions at their seats. The master explains, “Once the Demon King’s HP falls to half or below, its fighting style changes from the next telegraph onward.”
events.F5-40.name: The Outer Moat Chain Tavern
events.F5-40.scene: A removed drawbridge chain forms the back of a long bench. Service windows line an inner corridor overlooking the moat.
events.F5-40.action: Walk the corridor and choose where to rest or attend to your needs. Ask the bridge keeper about construction on the way to the castle.
events.F5-40.result: Rest on the bench, shop at the supply window, change jobs at the work window, or recruit companions at the bridge keeper’s seat. Ask the keeper to learn how many traps remain ahead through space 99. If none remain, the answer is 0.
events.F5-41.name: The Castle Smiths’ White Curtain
events.F5-41.scene: A shared workshop in town hangs a white curtain. Inside gather people offering baths, trade, job advice, and travel companionship.
events.F5-41.action: Open the workshop ledger and choose what you need. Before leaving, you can inspect armor with the master.
events.F5-41.result: Rest at the baths, shop in the trading area, change jobs at the advice desk, or recruit companions at the gathering table. During inspection, choose up to two owned armor pieces to compare their activation conditions and current defense.
events.F5-42.name: The Flagpole Bracket
events.F5-42.scene: A flagpole needs raising in the gate square. Fitting its bracket earns wages; helping with guard practice while the flag is supported earns armor.
events.F5-42.action: Secure the bracket to a board, or serve as a defender until the flag is raised.
events.F5-42.result: Fitting the bracket earns 640G. Serving as a defender grants AR44.
events.F5-43.name: The Bellows Maker’s Last Gust
events.F5-43.scene: A bellows maker divides leather between the current furnace and the next travelers. Work remains both in the workshop and delivering supplies.
events.F5-43.action: Pump the large bellows to finish a blade, or deliver leather to the aid station.
events.F5-43.result: The bellows cost 4 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grant SW45. The aid station grants one HE45.
events.F5-44.name: The Returning Soldier’s Checklist
events.F5-44.scene: A returning soldier counts fasteners left in a weapon crate. Before reporting, someone must replace loose ones and reconcile the count with the ledger.
events.F5-44.action: Use one AT46 to repair the crate and inspect every fastener, or take a break in the soldiers’ rest area.
events.F5-44.result: Repairs consume one AT46 and earn a one-time inspection payment of 520G. A break restores 6 HP and 2 MP. You can take a break without the item.
events.F5-45.name: The Gate Lamp’s Fire Bowl
events.F5-45.scene: The current fire bowl lasts only a night. Recoating it earns gold; resting with the keeper beside the fire comes with a warm meal.
events.F5-45.action: Recoat the fire bowl or eat with the keeper.
events.F5-45.result: Recoating costs 3 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and earns 720G. The meal restores 10 HP.
events.F5-46.name: The Mason’s Envelope
events.F5-46.scene: An envelope from a mason contains one receipt confirming a completed repair. It can be submitted to either the supply store or the armory, but not both.
events.F5-46.action: Choose the town’s supply store or armor store and hand over the receipt.
events.F5-46.result: The supply store grants one BD45. The armor store grants AR46.
events.F5-47.name: One Last Test for the Party
events.F5-47.scene: A tester calls out to the party heading for the gate. You may swing a heavy hammer or steady your defensive stance.
events.F5-47.action: Strike the sample with the hammer for combat supplies, or settle into your stance and rest.
events.F5-47.result: The hammer grants one AT47. Steadying your stance restores 5 HP and 4 MP.
events.F5-48.name: The Portcullis Return Rope
events.F5-48.scene: The end of the rope holding up the portcullis crosses the passage. A sign warns, “Do not step into the rope loop.”
events.F5-48.action: Pass beneath the portcullis outside the loop, or hurry through inside it.
events.F5-48.result: Going outside leaves you unharmed. Stepping into the loop catches your foot and costs 6 HP (minimum 1 remaining).
events.F5-49.name: Temporary Planks over the Moat
events.F5-49.scene: Wet temporary planks tilt to one side. A paid cart barge has arrived, though you could also check your footing and cross.
events.F5-49.action: Pay 200G for the barge, or carry your load across one plank at a time.
events.F5-49.result: The barge costs 200G and leaves you unharmed. Crossing the planks costs 5 HP (minimum 1 remaining). You can cross on your own without any gold.
events.F5-50.name: The Shutter’s Echo
events.F5-50.scene: Wind can slam the castle wall’s inspection window shut. A wooden wedge for holding it open lies on the sill beside you.
events.F5-50.action: Wedge the window open before looking through, or lean in without securing it.
events.F5-50.result: Using the wedge leaves you unharmed. Without it, the shutter’s bang startles you, costing 2 HP and 3 MP (minimum 1 HP and 0 MP remaining).

events.B1-01.name: A Board for Copying Tracks
events.B1-01.scene: A field watcher coats a board with charcoal beside some gnawed wheat.
events.B1-01.action: Copy the tracks accompanied by long, narrow sword marks and hand them over.
events.B1-02.name: The Shepherd’s Lost Bell
events.B1-02.scene: A bell from a sheep that jumped the fence is ringing beneath a bush.
events.B1-02.action: Pull out the bell by hand, or push it with a branch and roll it toward the ewe.
events.B1-02.result: Either way, the bell returns to its owner and you receive 180G. A branch keeps you clear of the thorns; using your bare hand costs 1 HP (minimum 1 remaining).
events.B1-03.name: The Gnawed Stake
events.B1-03.scene: A cart owner asks for help: “Just show me which stake had its rope chewed through.”
events.B1-03.action: Mark the stake with powdery wood shavings beside it.
events.B1-03.result: The correct stake gets a new rope, and you receive 220G. Choosing a stake without shavings earns nothing.
events.B1-04.name: The Roadside Leather Bag
events.B1-04.scene: Cut grass brings up a muddy bag tangled in the clippings.
events.B1-04.action: Match the brand on the bag’s corner to a lost-item notice in the roadside storage box.
events.B1-04.result: Choosing the matching wheat brand earns 160G from the owner. With a different mark, the bag stays in safekeeping and you receive no gold.
events.B1-05.name: Cleaning the Little Sword School
events.B1-05.scene: Wooden swords lie scattered over the field mice’s training ground, and their master cannot count them.
events.B1-05.action: Gather only the swords with split blades, or hurry onward.
events.B1-05.result: Gathering them earns 260G. Hurrying on costs nothing and gives no reward.
events.B1-06.name: The Lark Keeper’s Thanks
events.B1-06.scene: A hunter’s marker stands directly below a nest. The lark keeper wants it moved.
events.B1-06.action: Move the marker away from the nest and compare the tags for SW09 and SW02.
events.B1-06.result: Receive one chosen sword from the lark keeper.
events.B1-07.name: The Sisters Threading Armor
events.B1-07.scene: After tightening the woven grass, two sisters spread out their finished armor.
events.B1-07.action: Read the descriptions of AR09 and AR02 and choose which to thread with cord.
events.B1-07.result: Add the one armor piece you threaded to your inventory.
events.B1-08.name: The Last Weapon Shelf Before Moving
events.B1-08.scene: A hunter loads the final shelf onto a cart. There is no room for one last sword.
events.B1-08.action: Choose one sword to take from SW03, SW04, and SW05.
events.B1-08.result: Receive only the chosen sword. The others go on the next cart.
events.B1-09.name: Changing the Scarecrow’s Clothes
events.B1-09.scene: The field’s scarecrow wears layers of armor. The farmer wants to dress it in something finer.
events.B1-09.action: Choose one spare armor piece from AR03, AR04, and AR05.
events.B1-09.result: Receive the chosen armor. The newly dressed scarecrow stays in the field.
events.B1-10.name: The Apprentice Fixing the Fence
events.B1-10.scene: A fence stake is wobbling. An apprentice has been entrusted with a sample sword and armor.
events.B1-10.action: Reset the stake and choose SW06 or AR06 as your reward.
events.B1-10.result: Receive the one equipment piece you chose. The apprentice returns the other to the workshop.
events.B1-11.name: The Barn’s Name Tags
events.B1-11.scene: A bundle with a missing tag turns up in a barn. An order slip bearing the same family crest lies in the corner.
events.B1-11.action: Check the tags for SW07, SW08, AR07, and AR08, then specify the one item you will take.
events.B1-11.result: Receive the one equipment piece indicated by your mark on the order slip.
events.B1-12.name: Where the Wheat Bends
events.B1-12.scene: You cannot see the Field Mouse Swordsman’s ears, but trampled wheat bends stalk by stalk from the left.
events.B1-12.action: When first guarding, point your shield toward the falling wheat or in the opposite direction.
events.B1-12.result: Facing the wheat reduces the first thrust to 0 damage. Facing away or taking another action means receiving the telegraphed thrust normally. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-13.name: A Hoe on the Rounded Hill
events.B1-13.scene: A curled-up Armored Mole rolls down the slope just once. A sturdy hoe lies nearby.
events.B1-13.action: Guard on your first turn by thrusting the hoe into the slope, or hurry to attack.
events.B1-13.result: Guarding lifts its round armor onto the hoe: you take 0 damage and the enemy takes 3. Other actions leave you facing the telegraphed body slam. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-14.name: The Stuck Scabbard
events.B1-14.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman pulls at its long sword, but the scabbard clasp is still fastened.
events.B1-14.action: On your first turn, aim a normal attack at the clasp or the enemy’s body.
events.B1-14.result: Striking the clasp deals no damage this turn but weakens each of the enemy’s first two attacks by 2. Striking the body delivers a normal hit and opens the scabbard. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-15.name: Two Holes, One Above the Other
events.B1-15.scene: An Armored Mole spits soil through the upper hole and hides its tail in the lower one.
events.B1-15.action: Choose the upper or lower hole for your first normal attack.
events.B1-15.result: The lower hole hits the real body; the upper misses. Either way, both holes collapse at the end of that turn, leaving only the body as a target from the next turn onward. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-16.name: Nut-Shell Clappers
events.B1-16.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman strikes a pair of nuts. A sign reads, “Two clicks mean two thrusts.”
events.B1-16.action: Guard against the first turn’s double thrust, or attack first to wear the enemy down.
events.B1-16.result: Guarding reduces both thrusts to 0. With another action, a surviving enemy deals 2 damage twice. The nuts break this turn. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-17.name: One Sweet Potato for Lunch
events.B1-17.scene: An Armored Mole carries a roasted sweet potato at its waist. The first time its HP falls to half or below, it telegraphs that it will eat.
events.B1-17.action: On that turn, use a normal attack to knock away the potato or strike the body.
events.B1-17.result: Targeting the potato prevents all enemy healing. Targeting the body delivers a normal hit, after which a surviving enemy restores 4 HP. The potato is used once per battle. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-18.name: A Leafy Stand-In
events.B1-18.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman has put a hat on a straw dummy. Only one of the two has footprints beneath it.
events.B1-18.action: On your first attack, aim at the dummy or the opponent with footprints.
events.B1-18.result: The opponent with footprints takes 2 extra damage from the first hit. The dummy takes 0. Immediately afterward, the dummy falls and only the real body remains as a target. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-19.name: The Slice of Tree Stump
events.B1-19.scene: An Armored Mole strikes the stump’s roots. Cracks spread only beneath the slice of wood on which you stand.
events.B1-19.action: Step down from the stump before fighting, or ready yourself on top of it.
events.B1-19.result: Stepping down avoids the first turn’s ground fissure. Staying adds 3 to your first-turn normal attack, but a surviving enemy’s fissure deals 3 damage. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-20.name: The Dozing Sword Guard
events.B1-20.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman sleeps against a bell. Its cord stretches all the way to your feet.
events.B1-20.action: Remove the bell before fighting, or ring it and stand squarely before the guard.
events.B1-20.result: Removing it means the enemy only wakes up on turn 1. Ringing it lets the enemy act from the first turn, but its startled fumble drops a flask that restores 2 MP before battle. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-21.name: Half-Dried Mud Armor
events.B1-21.scene: The mud on an Armored Mole’s back has dried white, but its flank still gleams wet.
events.B1-21.action: Aim your first-turn normal attack at its white back or wet flank.
events.B1-21.result: The back takes 0 from this hit, but the mud cracks and enemy defense drops by 2 for the battle. The flank takes a normal hit immediately; the mud then dries and the choice disappears. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-22.name: A Duel beneath Chestnut Branches
events.B1-22.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman braces against a chestnut tree. One swing could shake its low branch.
events.B1-22.action: Strike the branch on your first turn, or slash directly at the swordsman.
events.B1-22.result: The branch drops chestnuts, dealing a fixed 4 damage to the enemy and a fixed 1 to you. Striking the body gives only a normal attack. All the chestnuts fall at once. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-23.name: The Dusty Air Hole
events.B1-23.scene: An Armored Mole has hidden underground. You can see air flowing toward its hole and the tracks where it will emerge.
events.B1-23.action: Use your first-turn normal attack to knock soil into the air hole, or use the moment to prepare yourself.
events.B1-23.result: Dropping soil deals 2 damage to the enemy. Other actions are available, but a strike at the body misses. The enemy does not attack on turn 1 and fights above ground from turn 2. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-24.name: The Wooden Target on Its Back
events.B1-24.scene: The target on a Field Mouse Swordsman’s back has as many holes as the die result that landed you here.
events.B1-24.action: Check the number before battle and pull the odd-numbered cord or the even-numbered cord.
events.B1-24.result: Matching the die result drops the target, letting your first normal attack ignore defense. A mismatch leaves it in place to reduce that hit by 2 before breaking. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-25.name: The Embankment Rope Ladder
events.B1-25.scene: An Armored Mole digs directly beneath a ladder. Climbing to a higher rung would let you strike with the momentum of a fall.
events.B1-25.action: Climb before battle or wait at the foot of the embankment.
events.B1-25.result: Climbing adds 3 to your first-turn normal attack, but if the enemy survives, landing costs 1 HP. You may still choose another action or flee after climbing; those choices cause no landing loss. Waiting below gives a normal battle. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-26.name: The Reverse-Grip Dagger
events.B1-26.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman grips its dagger backward, signaling, “Strike me and I strike back.”
events.B1-26.action: During the counterblade telegraph, make a normal attack or choose guard or an item.
events.B1-26.result: If your first-turn normal attack hits and the enemy survives, it returns 3 damage. Other actions make the counterblade miss. Normal telegraphs resume next turn. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-27.name: The Little Copper Windmill
events.B1-27.scene: An Armored Mole rests its forepaws on a windmill. Its turning blades draw up muddy water for protection.
events.B1-27.action: Stop the blades before battle, or push them backward and let the water wash over you.
events.B1-27.result: Stopping them prevents the mud and gives a normal battle. Reversing them restores 3 HP to you but coats the enemy in mud that absorbs up to 3 damage from the next hit. The mud falls away with that hit. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-28.name: The Grass Whistle Decoy
events.B1-28.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman has set down a signal whistle. It is preparing to blow it at the end of the first turn.
events.B1-28.action: Break the whistle with a normal attack, or use the turn to attack the enemy or prepare.
events.B1-28.result: Breaking it makes the first enemy action miss. Otherwise, the whistle reduces your MP by 2 (minimum 0 remaining). It can only be blown once. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-29.name: A Stone Slab Seesaw
events.B1-29.scene: An Armored Mole and a large rock sit at opposite ends of one stone slab. A wedge supports the rock.
events.B1-29.action: Remove the wedge before battle, or leave the footing level.
events.B1-29.result: Removing it starts the enemy at 4 below maximum HP (minimum 1), but you slip and lose 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining). Leaving it keeps both sides unchanged. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-30.name: Crossing the White Line Once
events.B1-30.scene: A Field Mouse Swordsman draws a white line in the grass. Only on the first turn crossing it will someone’s feet be exposed.
events.B1-30.action: Guard on the first turn and let the enemy cross, or step over yourself and strike.
events.B1-30.result: Guarding makes the enemy cross and adds 4 to your next normal attack. Attacking first deals a normal hit immediately but adds 2 to the enemy’s hit this turn. Other actions give no extra effect. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B1-31.name: The Watchtower Tube
events.B1-31.scene: A small sealed tube rolls out of a tilted watchtower.
events.B1-31.action: Pull the rope to bring the tube within reach.
events.B1-31.result: Receive the combat item inside: one AT01.
events.B1-32.name: A Path through Springy Grass
events.B1-32.scene: A guide has left two packages among grass that springs back up when trodden on.
events.B1-32.action: Think about your next moves and choose one item from BD01 and BD02.
events.B1-33.name: A Free Hand for the Herbalist
events.B1-33.scene: An herbalist holds a lamb in each arm and points toward a package at their waist.
events.B1-33.action: Set one lamb in the shoulder carrier and accept HE01 or HE02.
events.B1-33.result: Receive one chosen healing item in thanks for your help.
events.B1-34.name: A Hunter’s Note
events.B1-34.scene: A hunter’s note reads, “The left package is for battle; the right is for the road.”
events.B1-34.action: Choose AT03 on the left or BD03 on the right.
events.B1-34.result: Add one chosen item to your inventory and leave the other for the next traveler.
events.B1-35.name: Loose Stable Straw
events.B1-35.scene: Two undamaged supply boxes turn up in the stable bedding.
events.B1-35.action: Check the stable keeper’s mark and take either HE04 or AT04.
events.B1-35.result: Receive one of the chosen item.
events.B1-36.name: A Freshly Drawn Bucket
events.B1-36.scene: A child offers to lower the well bucket once for you.
events.B1-36.action: Drink from the dipper or cool your forehead.
events.B1-36.result: Drinking restores 5 HP; cooling your forehead restores 3 MP. Choose only one.
events.B1-37.name: A Warm Box for Chicks
events.B1-37.scene: You hold a box of wind-chilled chicks beneath a blanket. The hot-water bottle is still warm.
events.B1-37.action: Warm your hands and the chicks, then return the box to their parent.
events.B1-37.result: Restore 3 HP and 1 MP, each up to its maximum.
events.B1-38.name: A Cow Shares the Shade
events.B1-38.scene: While grazing, a cow leaves half the shade beneath a tree free for you.
events.B1-38.action: Use a tree root as a pillow and take a short rest.
events.B1-38.result: Restore half your missing HP, rounded up. At full HP, you gain nothing.
events.B1-39.name: The Inn Where Hounds Return
events.B1-39.scene: When a little bell rings at the door, a hound bounds up and the innkeeper sets out four signs.
events.B1-39.action: Choose to rest in a bed, browse the shop, change jobs, recruit a companion, or depart.
events.B1-39.result: The dog’s find is available only once. If your bag is empty, receive one AT09; otherwise, play with the dog to restore 2 HP. Rest here for free once to restore half your maximum HP and half your maximum MP. Shopping, job changes, and companion recruitment are also available. Choose departure to finish.
events.B1-40.name: The Hay-Roofed Inn
events.B1-40.scene: An herbalist and a peddler shelter from rain beneath the hay roof. Job notices line the hearth.
events.B1-40.action: Rest, shop, change jobs, or recruit a companion, then depart when ready.
events.B1-40.result: Once while sheltering, you can trade one owned BD08 for one HE08. Without it, you can still use the facilities without trading. Rest here for free once to restore half your maximum HP and half your maximum MP. Shopping, job changes, and companion recruitment are also available. Choose departure to finish.
events.B1-41.name: The Weathercock Watch House
events.B1-41.scene: The night watchman lays job and trade notices on the table and offers you an empty chair.
events.B1-41.action: Lie down, visit the shop, change jobs, recruit a companion, or move on.
events.B1-41.result: Consult the watchman’s ledger once to learn the next gold space’s number and the amount it can grant. If none lies ahead, it shows “None.” Rest here for free once to restore half your maximum HP and half your maximum MP. Shopping, job changes, and companion recruitment are also available. Choose departure to finish.
events.B1-42.name: The Shepherd’s Lead Rope
events.B1-42.scene: A lost sheep refuses to cross a shallow ditch. Its shepherd offers payment or first aid.
events.B1-42.action: Carry it across or lure it with feed.
events.B1-42.result: Carrying it costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and earns 230G. Luring it earns no gold, but the shepherd washes your wounds to restore 4 HP.
events.B1-43.name: The Injured Watchbird
events.B1-43.scene: A watchbird huddles beside its nest. Its owner has a reward ready.
events.B1-43.action: Give one HE03 if you have it, or fetch water for the bird.
events.B1-43.result: Giving the package consumes one HE03 and grants one AT05. Fetching water consumes nothing and also restores 2 HP to you.
events.B1-44.name: The Hunter’s Two Maps
events.B1-44.scene: A hunter keeps maps of “the next prey” and “the next inn” rolled separately.
events.B1-44.action: Unroll just one and memorize its mark.
events.B1-44.result: Prey reveals the nearest battle space ahead; the inn map reveals the nearest inn you have not yet passed. If no matching space lies ahead, “None” appears before you choose.
events.B1-45.name: A Gap in the Cart
events.B1-45.scene: A cartwright says there is room for one package in an empty wheel support.
events.B1-45.action: Buy BD04 for 27G, or help push the cart without buying.
events.B1-45.result: Buying costs 27G and grants one BD04. Pushing costs and grants no items, but restores 2 HP. You can push if you lack the gold.
events.B1-46.name: Morning Practice beyond the Stakes
events.B1-46.scene: A master raises a bundle of grass and asks, “Strike harder, or steady your footing?”
events.B1-46.action: Choose sword practice or shield practice.
events.B1-46.result: For the next battle only, sword practice adds 2 damage to your first normal attack; shield practice reduces the first positive damage you take by 2. The effect ends when the battle does.
events.B1-47.name: The Hound’s Chosen Packages
events.B1-47.scene: A hound wags its tail with two packages in its mouth. One is meant for the watch post.
events.B1-47.action: Deliver the earth-colored package or the white one.
events.B1-47.result: Delivering the earth-colored package earns the remaining HE05. Delivering white earns the remaining BD05. Receive one item.
events.B1-48.name: The Rattle Alarm Rope
events.B1-48.scene: A rattle-alarm rope hides in the grass just before the stepping stones.
events.B1-48.action: Pay 80G to have the rope removed, or kneel and crawl beneath it.
events.B1-48.result: Removal costs 80G; crawling costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining). Using one substitute ticket avoids both costs.
events.B1-49.name: Sticky Straw Sandals
events.B1-49.scene: Sticky bird-repellent sap has spilled on the path. Grass clings to your sandals whenever you lift a foot.
events.B1-49.action: Pay the sand seller 90G, or pull your sandals free by hand.
events.B1-49.result: Sand costs 90G. Pulling by hand costs 2 MP (minimum 0 remaining). One substitute ticket avoids the loss.
events.B1-50.name: The Empty Prey Basket
events.B1-50.scene: A fallen basket’s spring has caught only the strap of your pack.
events.B1-50.action: Wedge the spring with one of your items, or lift it with your shoulder.
events.B1-50.result: Lose one specified consumable, or spend 3 HP (minimum 1 remaining). A substitute ticket consumes just one ticket, sparing your other items and HP.

events.B2-01.name: The Sluice Patrol Tag
events.B2-01.scene: Crab bubbles gather at just one of three gates by the landing. A boatman is looking for a blockage.
events.B2-01.action: Point out the gate with the bubbles and scoop out the waterweed with a net.
events.B2-02.name: The Upside-Down Fish Basket
events.B2-02.scene: A fish basket bearing a fisherman’s mark floats past upside down where a narrow stream joins a wider one.
events.B2-02.action: Wait at the confluence, or pull it in with your own rope tied to the bank.
events.B2-02.result: Waiting returns the basket for 240G. The rope earns the same 240G and reveals the next normal-battle enemy’s name, but hauling costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining).
events.B2-03.name: Wet Price Tags at the Morning Market
events.B2-03.scene: Overnight flooding washed three price tags from a shelf. A thumb-sized crab clutches one.
events.B2-03.action: Match the pictures to the goods and return the crab’s shellfish tag to the shellfish basket.
events.B2-03.result: The shellfish basket earns 340G. At another basket, the shopkeeper corrects you and pays nothing.
events.B2-04.name: Stones at the Ferry Crossing
events.B2-04.scene: Round footprints vanish into the water, leaving only stones above the surface. The ferryman wants to mark a safe route.
events.B2-04.action: Check the shallow places one by one, or simply watch.
events.B2-04.result: Checking costs 3 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and earns 420G for the record. Watching changes nothing.
events.B2-05.name: The Mussel Receipt Tag
events.B2-05.scene: A supplier has lost track of who advanced the ferry fare. The wooden tags floating nearby have writing on their backs too.
events.B2-05.action: Turn the tags over and give the boatman the one marked “Advance.”
events.B2-05.result: The correct tag earns 200G. Choosing “Paid” leaves no outstanding debt and earns nothing.
events.B2-06.name: Lost Packages beneath the Raft
events.B2-06.scene: Two wrapped swords are caught beneath a raft tied to a post.
events.B2-06.action: Use a rope from the bank to draw in SW11, or enter the water to retrieve SW12.
events.B2-06.result: SW11 grants only that sword. SW12 costs 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining), grants that sword, and restores 1 MP.
events.B2-07.name: The Hermit Crab’s Empty Box
events.B2-07.scene: A little hermit crab peeks out of a seemingly empty box. A fisherman wants a net for drying armor repaired.
events.B2-07.action: Compare AR11 and AR12, or pass up the items and repair the net.
events.B2-07.result: Receive one chosen armor piece. Repairing the net grants no equipment, but the fisherman’s herbal drink restores 5 HP.
events.B2-08.name: The Regatta Prize Rack
events.B2-08.scene: The riverboat race has ended, leaving unredeemed prize tags hanging from a broken flagpole.
events.B2-08.action: Repair the flagpole and bring the weaver one sword tag: SW13, SW14, or SW15.
events.B2-08.result: Receive the matching sword. The tag is collected and cannot be redeemed again.
events.B2-09.name: The Float Maker’s Fitting Stand
events.B2-09.scene: A tank for testing armor weight has lines marked “Shallow” and “Deep.” The craftsperson presents two samples.
events.B2-09.action: Choose AR13 at the shallow line or AR14 at the deep line, then leave the fitting stand.
events.B2-09.result: AR13 grants that armor and restores 1 HP. AR14 grants that armor and restores 1 MP.
events.B2-10.name: The Low-Tide Smithy Boat
events.B2-10.scene: The smithy boat’s lower shelf is reachable only while the water is low. Your landing die result indicates the water level.
events.B2-10.action: On a roll of 1–3, choose SW16 or AR15 from below. On 4–6, choose SW17 or AR16 from above.
events.B2-10.result: Receive one equipment piece from the reachable shelf. The die result and both candidates appear before you collect it.
events.B2-11.name: The Fishing Master’s Rented Storehouse
events.B2-11.scene: A fishing master is clearing away old boat parts. A heavy stone rests against the door at the back.
events.B2-11.action: Take AR17 from the front, or move the stone to choose SW18 or AR18 from the back.
events.B2-11.result: The front grants AR17. Reaching the back costs 3 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grants one chosen equipment piece.
events.B2-12.name: The Discarded Shell
events.B2-12.scene: An identical empty shell lies beside a Shallows Crab. Only the real crab blows bubbles beneath its belly.
events.B2-12.action: Aim at the real crab on your first turn, or deliberately crush the empty shell and collect its fragments.
events.B2-12.result: The bubbling crab takes a normal hit. The empty shell takes your first strike without damaging the enemy, but its fragments block up to 4 of the next damage you take this battle. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-13.name: An Echo at the Sluice
events.B2-13.scene: A Glowtail Bat sends its cry toward the sluice wall. A carving shows the sound returning when the gate is shut.
events.B2-13.action: Close the sluice before battle or leave it open.
events.B2-13.result: Closing it reflects the first turn’s cry for 3 enemy damage and 0 damage to you. However, the enemy’s glow is hidden, weakening your first-turn normal attack by 2. Leaving it open gives a normal battle. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-14.name: Two Colors of Claw Cord
events.B2-14.scene: A Shallows Crab has a herbal-drink pouch tied to its right claw and a bag of throwing stones on its left.
events.B2-14.action: Use your first-turn normal attack to cut one cord or aim at the body.
events.B2-14.result: Cutting right leaves only a fixed 3-damage stone attack on the enemy’s first turn. Cutting left leaves only 3 HP of enemy healing. Striking the body gives a normal hit, after which a living enemy uses both. The bags last only for the first turn. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-15.name: The Oil-Dish Light Keeper
events.B2-15.scene: A Glowtail Bat absorbs light from an oil dish. Two drops remain, with one spent on each use.
events.B2-15.action: Tip the dish with a normal attack on turn 1 or 2, or attack directly.
events.B2-15.result: Targeting the dish deals 0 damage to the enemy. While oil remains, the enemy restores 3 HP at the end of each turn and consumes one drop. A defeated enemy does not heal. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-16.name: The Crab on the Tilting Plank
events.B2-16.scene: The shoreward and riverward ends of the Shallows Crab’s plank sink alternately. The riverward end starts higher.
events.B2-16.action: For normal attacks during the first two turns, step on the displayed high side or low side.
events.B2-16.result: The high side deals normal damage. The low side reduces your damage dealt by 2 but also reduces damage you take that turn by 2. The plank reaches shore on turn 3. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-17.name: A Mouth in the Water Mirror
events.B2-17.scene: The Glowtail Bat’s face is dark, but its mouth shines in the water’s reflection. The closed-mouth symbol signals a draining bite.
events.B2-17.action: Guard against the first turn’s “Draining Bite,” or attack despite the danger.
events.B2-17.result: Guarding makes the bite fail and prevents enemy healing. Otherwise, the enemy restores as much HP as the damage it actually deals. This move occurs once. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-18.name: The Rope Holding You to Shore
events.B2-18.scene: A Shallows Crab hooks its claw over the boat’s edge. If the boat moves away, it will be left over the river.
events.B2-18.action: Untie the shore rope first to gain distance, or leave it tied and fight close up.
events.B2-18.result: Untying it puts both sides’ normal attacks out of reach on turn 1, but spells, items, and guarding remain available. The boat reaches the opposite bank on turn 2. Leaving it tied keeps all actions in reach from the start. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-19.name: The Watch Desk’s Light Window
events.B2-19.scene: A Glowtail Bat follows the light. Beyond a small window sits a shelf where you can lay out your bag’s contents.
events.B2-19.action: Use one item on your first turn and step into the shelf’s shadow, or fight in front of the window.
events.B2-19.result: Using an item consumes one as normal, and the window frame blocks the enemy’s hit that turn for 0 damage. Other actions get no protection. The window closes at the end of turn 1. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-20.name: The Bubble-Guarded Pearl
events.B2-20.scene: Three bubbles cling to a pearl held by a Shallows Crab. One bubble breaks with each hit.
events.B2-20.action: Break the bubbles one hit at a time, or aim one normal attack at the pearl to clear them all.
events.B2-20.result: Each bubble reduces one hit to the body by 2. Targeting the pearl deals 0 enemy damage and removes every remaining bubble. No new bubbles form. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-21.name: Shadows on the Stone Bridge
events.B2-21.scene: A Glowtail Bat’s wings cast three shadows on the wall. The bridge rail reads, “Light the shadow facing the fish.”
events.B2-21.action: Before battle, light one lantern marked fish, boat, or house.
events.B2-21.result: Fish changes the enemy’s first powerful attack into a normal attack. Boat or house leaves it unchanged, but leftover oil restores 2 MP to you. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-22.name: The Basket Sinking on One Side
events.B2-22.scene: The stone supporting a Shallows Crab’s fish basket is slowly slipping underwater.
events.B2-22.action: Push the stone with your first-turn normal attack, or strike the enemy atop the springy basket.
events.B2-22.result: Pushing the stone deals 0 damage, but the enemy falls at the end of turn 2 for a fixed 6 damage. Striking the body gives a normal hit immediately; the basket then reaches shore and does not fall. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-23.name: White Cloth on the Washboard
events.B2-23.scene: You can lift a large white cloth before the Glowtail Bat opens its eyes.
events.B2-23.action: Stretch the cloth to scatter the light, or leave it lowered and gather your magic.
events.B2-23.result: The raised cloth reduces the enemy’s first light move this battle to 0, but also reduces your first attack spell’s damage by 2. Lowering it restores 2 MP before a normal battle. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-24.name: The Scale-Shaped Sluice Board
events.B2-24.scene: A Shallows Crab crouches before the sluice board. One red knot marks the gate rope.
events.B2-24.action: Tie the rope short before battle, or leave it long.
events.B2-24.result: A short rope releases water at the start of turn 2; a long rope releases it at the start of turn 3. The water deals a fixed 5 enemy damage. Winning before then gives no extra damage. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-25.name: Napping beneath the Boat
events.B2-25.scene: A Glowtail Bat hangs beneath the boat. It rests in the light and flies when it grows dark.
events.B2-25.action: Open or close the skylight before battle.
events.B2-25.result: Open: the enemy does not attack on turn 1, instead restoring 4 HP. Closed: it attacks immediately, but starts startled at 4 below maximum HP (minimum 1). Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-26.name: Balancing the Claw
events.B2-26.scene: A stone weight hangs from a Shallows Crab’s large claw. The stone rises during its “Wind Up” telegraph.
events.B2-26.action: During that telegraph, guard to catch the stone or make a normal attack at the exposed side.
events.B2-26.result: On the first occurrence only, guarding knocks off the weight and weakens all later enemy normal attacks by 2. Attacking adds 4 to that hit but leaves the weight attached. Other actions add nothing. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-27.name: Light between the Boat Planks
events.B2-27.scene: A Glowtail Bat peers through a gap in the boat. Moving the light right illuminates the left plank.
events.B2-27.action: Before battle, study the wet- and dry-plank pictures and place the light to illuminate the dry plank.
events.B2-27.result: Lighting the dry plank gives secure footing: immediately after your first positive damage taken, counter for a fixed 3 enemy damage if you survive. Lighting the wet plank gives no counter. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-28.name: A Chip from the Ice Seller
events.B2-28.scene: Ice falls from a seller’s boat and breaks into a piece small enough for the Shallows Crab to pinch.
events.B2-28.action: Slide the ice over with your first-turn normal attack, or attack the body first.
events.B2-28.result: Choosing ice makes the enemy grip it on turn 1: you deal and take 0 damage. During only the next enemy hit, guarding also restores 3 MP. The ice then melts. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-29.name: One Turn of the Waterwheel
events.B2-29.scene: A Glowtail Bat’s shadow approaches the waterwheel window. For just the first two turns, the window’s front and back alternate.
events.B2-29.action: Make a normal attack on turn 1, or wait to attack on turn 2 when the back faces you.
events.B2-29.result: A turn-1 normal attack loses 2 damage to the window frame. A turn-2 normal attack catches a wing for 3 extra damage. Other turns and actions are unchanged. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-30.name: The One-Way Ferry
events.B2-30.scene: A Glowtail Bat boards the ferry. You may borrow just one pole from the boatman.
events.B2-30.action: Choose “Sweep” to use the pole for your first attack, or “Support” to use it for your first healing.
events.B2-30.result: Sweep adds 2 to your first normal attack. Support adds 3 HP of healing on the first turn you use a combat healing item. Either benefit occurs only once in this battle. Victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP, with separate equipment and item drop rolls. Fleeing or losing grants no battle rewards.
events.B2-31.name: Messages in the Net Knots
events.B2-31.scene: The master’s knot code is “one for the boat, two for treatment.” Two bags bear these marks.
events.B2-31.action: Choose BD11 with one knot or HE11 with two.
events.B2-31.result: Receive one item from your chosen bag.
events.B2-32.name: Drying Supplies after a Shower
events.B2-32.scene: Packages labeled AT12 and AT13 are drying in the boathouse. Only one shelf can fit beneath the roof.
events.B2-32.action: Move the roof over AT12 or AT13.
events.B2-32.result: Receive one combat item from the covered side. The shopkeeper dries the wet side again.
events.B2-33.name: Unloading the Reed Boat
events.B2-33.scene: A cargo owner needs one small parcel each of healing, travel, and combat supplies carried ashore.
events.B2-33.action: Read the HE13, BD13, and AT14 tags, then carry one parcel.
events.B2-33.result: The owner gives you one of the item you carried.
events.B2-34.name: Packages in the Waterway
events.B2-34.scene: Oil-paper-wrapped cargo floats along a shallow waterway. A long net lies on the bank; a short net rests on the stepping stones.
events.B2-34.action: Take the HE14 parcel from the bank, or stand on the stones to take the BD14 parcel.
events.B2-34.result: The bank grants one HE14. The stones cost 2 HP (minimum 1 remaining) and grant one BD14.
events.B2-35.name: Today’s Rescue Box
events.B2-35.scene: A sign on the ferry’s rescue box gives priority to travelers with empty bags.
events.B2-35.action: Check your total item count and decide what to receive.
events.B2-35.result: With 0 items, receive one HE15 and one AT15. With at least 1 item, choose one of those two and receive one.
events.B2-36.name: Warm Stones from the Riverbed
events.B2-36.scene: The boatman warms a stone in hot water for you. You can warm your feet or eyelids in turn.
events.B2-36.action: Keep it at your feet longer, or at your eyelids longer.
events.B2-36.result: Feet restore 6 HP and 1 MP; eyelids restore 2 HP and 4 MP, up to their maximums.
events.B2-37.name: One Cup in the Strainer
events.B2-37.scene: Just one cup remains at the herbal tea stall. “The strong brew is for the weary,” says the owner.
events.B2-37.action: Check your current HP and drink the tea.
events.B2-37.result: If your HP is half or below immediately before drinking, restore 8 HP. Otherwise, restore 4 MP.
events.B2-38.name: The Boat’s Mooring Post
events.B2-38.scene: A small resting boat is tied to a post rocking with the waves. Winding in the rope would steady it.
events.B2-38.action: Lie down while it rocks, or wind in the rope first.
events.B2-38.result: Resting as it is restores 4 HP. Winding the rope costs 1 MP and restores 8 HP. Without enough MP, you can rest without winding it.
events.B2-39.name: The Ferryman’s Teahouse
events.B2-39.scene: A water-level chart hangs on the teahouse wall. At the neighboring table, someone waits to help with travel preparations.
events.B2-39.action: Use the inn’s four facilities and check the water-level chart once before departing.
events.B2-39.result: The chart shows the numbers and enemy names of battle spaces within the next 6 spaces. If there are none, it says, “None in the next 6 spaces.” Rest here for free once to restore half your maximum HP and half your maximum MP. Shopping, job changes, and companion recruitment are also available. Choose departure to finish.
events.B2-40.name: The Reed Pier Hotel
events.B2-40.scene: The innkeeper writes tonight’s bath options on two tags that washed ashore.
events.B2-40.action: Use the facilities freely. When resting, choose a footbath or hand bath.
events.B2-40.result: In addition to normal rest, the footbath restores 2 extra HP or the hand bath restores 2 extra MP, up to the maximum. This bonus occurs once, when resting at this inn. Rest here for free once to restore half your maximum HP and half your maximum MP. Shopping, job changes, and companion recruitment are also available. Choose departure to finish.
events.B2-41.name: The Sluice Watch Inn
events.B2-41.scene: The watch inn has a boat-supply shop, a tavern, and an old picture map on the wall.
events.B2-41.action: Between resting, shopping, changing jobs, and recruiting, point to one picture that interests you.
events.B2-41.result: The blade reveals the next equipment space’s number; the bag reveals the next item space’s number. It also shows if none exists. Use the map only once per visit. Rest here for free once to restore half your maximum HP and half your maximum MP. Shopping, job changes, and companion recruitment are also available. Choose departure to finish.
events.B2-42.name: Waiting for the Thread Spool
events.B2-42.scene: A boatman untangles twisted thread. “Light it with magic, or use a tool if you’re in a hurry,” he says.
events.B2-42.action: Spend 2 MP to light the work, or rest here.
events.B2-42.result: Lighting it costs 2 MP and earns 360G. Resting restores 2 HP and 2 MP. You can rest without enough MP.
events.B2-43.name: The Found Bubble Whistle
events.B2-43.scene: A fishing master says the whistle can summon a Shallows Crab, though you may return it to the river instead.
events.B2-43.action: Blow it and fight, or return it to the river.
events.B2-43.result: Blowing it starts a normal battle against EN03. Only victory grants enemy-specific gold and XP plus equipment and item drop rolls; fleeing or losing gives no battle rewards. Returning it avoids battle and restores 3 MP.
events.B2-44.name: Boat Ticket or Treatment Ticket
events.B2-44.scene: A boat-inn vendor offers to tear off just one half of a paired ticket.
events.B2-44.action: Take the boat ticket or treatment ticket.
events.B2-44.result: The boat ticket grants one BD16. The treatment ticket grants one HE16, or you may decline the item to restore 6 HP here.
events.B2-45.name: Water Sold by the Flask
events.B2-45.scene: A water seller’s bucket holds exactly six sips of magic-restoring water.
events.B2-45.action: Buy it all for 120G, or take only a free taste.
events.B2-45.result: Buying costs 120G and restores 6 MP. Tasting costs nothing and restores 1 MP. You can taste without enough gold.
events.B2-46.name: The Fisherman Lending Fins
events.B2-46.scene: A fisherman prepares to swim upstream. He needs support either in the shallows or in deep water.
events.B2-46.action: Hold the shallows net or the deep-water marker.
events.B2-46.result: Shallows reduce the enemy’s normal attack by 3 on the first turn of the next battle only. Deep water adds 4 damage to your attack spell on that first turn only. The effect ends with the battle.
events.B2-47.name: The Anchor Logbook
events.B2-47.scene: A boatbuilder closes an anchor log and offers a silver bookmark and a flask.
events.B2-47.action: Put the bookmark in your bag, or drink the water and leave room in your bag.
events.B2-47.result: The bookmark grants one AT17. Water adds no item but restores 4 HP and 2 MP.
events.B2-48.name: Waves beneath the Pier Planks
events.B2-48.scene: As waves approach, the pier planks float up one by one. A boat keeper offers a balance pole.
events.B2-48.action: Rent the pole for 100G, or cross the wet shoreline stones.
events.B2-48.result: The pole costs 100G. On the stones, your landing roll costs 2 HP for 1–3 or 4 HP for 4–6 (minimum 1 remaining). One substitute ticket leaves you unharmed.
events.B2-49.name: The Fishhook beneath the Basket
events.B2-49.scene: As you step over a broken-bottomed fish basket, a rusty hook snags your pack.
events.B2-49.action: Cut the line, or reweave the basket to free yourself.
events.B2-49.result: Cutting costs 3 HP (minimum 1 remaining). Reweaving costs 2 MP (minimum 0 remaining). One substitute ticket avoids all other losses.
events.B2-50.name: Algae on the Boat’s Floor
events.B2-50.scene: Walking on the algae tilts the boat. A handled cargo weight rolls at your feet.
events.B2-50.action: Hold the weight still, or replace the rope with a new one.
events.B2-50.result: Holding it costs 4 HP (minimum 1 remaining). Replacing the rope costs 130G. One substitute ticket keeps the boat steady and spares both HP and gold.
